column1: # Triage of the differences in REPORT.md, one line per jurisdiction and
# figure: jurisdiction, figure, kind, reference, note, separated by tabs.
# kind is ours (a taxcalcs bug; reference is the issue), theirs (a
# PolicyEngine-US bug; reference is the upstream issue), reading (both
# readings are defensible; reference cites the form or law ours follows), or
# unmodeled (our rules take the figure as an input rather than computing it,
# and the households supply none; reference is the form line). Unmodeled rows
# are where a case running ahead of the rules is worth writing.

column5: The households paid no state income tax during 2025 (none withheld, no estimates), so Schedule A line 5a has nothing to deduct and they take the standard deduction. PolicyEngine-US deducts the year's state income tax liability as if paid, itemizes, and so reports lower taxable income and tax. Under $100,000 of taxable income the line 16 tax also differs by up to a few dollars because ours reads the Tax Table, as the instructions require, and PolicyEngine-US applies the rate formula to the exact amount.
As for tax_line_16: PolicyEngine-US deducts state income tax that was never paid.

Retirees: ours takes Form 40 page 2 Part I income, where a taxable pension goes, as AlabamaInputs.other_income, which the harness leaves empty, so the pension is left out as if from an exempt defined benefit plan. PolicyEngine-US taxes it as a private plan less the $6,000 exemption at 65. The harness does not say which kind of plan it is.

Workers: ours takes the Schedule A total as AlabamaInputs.itemized_deductions, which the harness leaves empty, so line 11 is the standard deduction. PolicyEngine-US itemizes, deducting employee Social Security and Medicare tax under Ala. Code 40-18-15(a)(3). Retirees: ours takes Form 40 page 2 Part I income, where a taxable pension goes, as AlabamaInputs.other_income, which the harness leaves empty, so the pension is left out as if from an exempt defined benefit plan. PolicyEngine-US taxes it as a private plan less the $6,000 exemption at 65. The harness does not say which kind of plan it is.

Ours has no line 18B, so a joint return takes one $6,000 retirement exemption instead of one for each spouse (ar-5).

Ours leaves the MCTCP worksheet out of line 36, so the federal senior deduction is not subtracted (az-2, az-5).

Follows agi.

Ours takes the pension and eligible retirement income exclusion as DelawareInputs.pension_exclusion, which the harness leaves empty. PolicyEngine-US excludes pensions and, at 60 and over, interest (de-2, de-4, de-5).

de-1, de-3: PolicyEngine-US files the couples as married filing combined separate when that is cheaper; ours files jointly, the election the harness makes. de-2, de-4, de-5 follow agi.

The IA 1040 starts from federal taxable income and has no Iowa AGI line; ours reports federal AGI. PolicyEngine-US reports federal AGI less the Iowa modifications (ia-2, ia-5). The tax agrees.

Line 4 adds lines 2 and 3 with no floor at zero, so ours carries a negative figure when the Social Security and retirement subtractions exceed federal taxable income (ia-2, ia-5). PolicyEngine-US floors it at zero. The tax is $0 both ways.

column5: ks-5: line 7 is $55,093; the Married Filing Joint column of the $55,051-$55,100 row prints $2,898, which ours gives. PolicyEngine-US applies the rate schedule ($2,899.39) below $100,000. Upstream issue not filed.

Retirees (ky-2, ky-5): ours does not compute the pension exclusion of up to $31,110 a person and says so in the KY_PENSION_EXCLUSION_NOT_COMPUTED diagnostic; it is a Schedule M subtraction input, which the harness leaves empty. PolicyEngine-US computes it.

ky-2, ky-5 follow agi. ky-1, ky-3: PolicyEngine-US files the couples as married filing separately on a combined return (status 2), with a standard deduction in each column; ours files jointly in column B, the election the harness makes.

Ours reports Form 1 line 10, the 5.0% income, which leaves out the interest that goes to line 20 from Schedule B. PolicyEngine-US's state_agi includes it (ma-1, ma-3, ma-4, ma-5). The interest is taxed the same in both.
PolicyEngine-US gives state_taxable_income as $0 for every Massachusetts household; its Massachusetts taxable incomes are kept in separate Part A, B and C variables. The tax agrees for the workers.

ma-2, ma-5: the 2025 Form 1 line 2c age 65 exemption is $1,700 each, which ours uses. PolicyEngine-US uses $700, so its tax is $50 higher a person. Upstream issue not filed. The workers' differences were the missing W-2 boxes 4 and 6, fixed in the harness.

Ours takes the pension exclusion (line 10a) and the two-income subtraction (line 14) as MarylandInputs, which the harness leaves empty. PolicyEngine-US computes both (md-1, md-3 two-income; md-2, md-5 pension).

Follows agi.

Retirees mn-2 and mn-5. Ours takes Schedule M1M subtractions as an input (Form M1 line 7, instructions PDF page 15), and the harness gives none; PolicyEngine-US works the Social Security subtraction ($23,205 for mn-5).

Retirees mn-2 and mn-5 as for taxable_income. Two-earner couple mn-1: ours takes Schedule M1C nonrefundable credits as an input (line 16, instructions PDF page 17), and PolicyEngine-US works the M1MA marriage credit ($452.07).
mo-4, $1.12: line 13's federal income tax deduction is a share of the federal tax, where ours reads the federal Tax Table and PolicyEngine-US the exact rate formula.

mo-5, retired couple: ours puts the spouse's pension, interest and Social Security in column Y (line 1S counts only W-2 wages), so line 26 is taxed in one column. PolicyEngine-US splits by person, as the line 1 worksheet (instructions PDF page 7) asks.

Two-earner couples ms-1 and ms-3: ours taxes the couple in column A alone, with one $10,000 zero-rate amount. PolicyEngine-US gives each spouse one, as the Schedule of Tax Computation (instructions PDF page 27) and line 17 (PDF page 7) do.

Retirees nc-2 and nc-5: the D-400 has no North Carolina AGI line. Ours reports line 8 minus line 9, which takes out taxable Social Security, and PolicyEngine-US reports federal AGI. Taxable income agrees.

Retirees nj-2 and nj-5. Ours takes the pension exclusion and other retirement income exclusion as inputs (instructions PDF page 22), and the harness gives none; PolicyEngine-US works both ($44,000 and $8,929 for nj-5).
As for agi.

Retirees ok-2 and ok-5. Ours takes Schedule 511-A subtractions as an input (Form 511 line 2), and the harness gives none; PolicyEngine-US works the Social Security and retirement subtractions ($55,700 for ok-5).

As for agi.
